cells.tense: A message or a request arrives today and you decide whether it comes in and stays.
cells.ask: Take the next thing that comes in — a message, a request, a chance — and answer it inside the hour. Say what it's for before you take it on. If you mean to carry it, tell one person. If you don't, say that plainly.
cells.core:
Something comes in from outside, and you're the one who decides whether it gets carried and what it's for. A request, something someone tells you, a chance that lands today. Different shapes, same moment. You can take one thing and mean it, and turn down the next, and that turning-down is what makes the yes worth anything.

Know what holds it up. This lasts while you answer things while they're still open. Let them settle into a shape of their own first, and the decision gets made around you.

A request lands in the next while. Answer it while it's still live. Say what you're taking on before you take it. Pick it up because you picked it.

The pen stays in your hand.

cells.tense: You are gripping an outcome that has not arrived, rehearsing the ending before the thing has begun.
cells.ask: Pick the outcome you most want to pin down and leave it alone for one day. Then write one plain sentence about the person or situation in front of you — what's actually there, not what it might become — and don't rewrite it.
cells.core:
You're at the door where things arrive, and you're ahead of it. Nothing has landed yet, most of it hasn't even been decided, and you're already managing how it ends, steering, pre-answering. The grip feels like care, and it's why the waiting is unbearable.

The other side of this is seeing the whole thing while you're inside it — a way of knowing that keeps opening instead of closing on a verdict. That kind of seeing has no finish line to force. Leave one outcome you've been managing alone for a day. Put one present thing into one plain sentence — what's in front of you now, not its possible versions — and leave it.

Both hands are on the door. That's why nothing can get through it.

cells.tense: You have been reading the grain of a door you already walked past, as if it were in front of you.
cells.ask: Choose the smallest thing coming today — a reply, a ten-minute task — and take it only because you picked it, with one way to know it's done. Then stand up and change rooms, and let it be finished.
cells.core:
What comes in from outside should meet someone picking it up. Nobody's there at the door to take it. Whatever you think about any of it, the standing-still is the whole of what's happening, and what arrives gets handled like something done to you rather than something you took.

Not choosing isn't something harder work fixes. The hands are already empty of it, and there's no strain that fills them. What's alive is elsewhere in you — the shining that doesn't need anyone's permission, that's already yours and doesn't need proving.

Take the smallest thing coming today. Take it because you picked it, and know one way you'll see it's done. Then stand up, change rooms, and leave it behind you.

You are someone who chooses. That hasn't been deleted.

cells.tense: The pen has been down for a while and the page kept moving without you noticing it move.
cells.ask: Take one choice you made today and say out loud who made it — plain, to yourself or someone else. Then do the next thing, and say the same while you're doing it.
cells.core:
Things are coming through your door and getting sorted — that sorting is running. You just don't have your hand on it, so it reads as drift. Parts of what's piled up look like outcomes you merely walked into. Parts of it you did: you went there, you kept it, you let the other thing go.

Here's what doesn't need a bigger life to change. What's already yours doesn't need proving or defending, only saying plainly. The same strength is available through a smaller moment, and it works the same either way.

Take a choice you made today and say out loud who made it. Say it once. Then do the next thing and say it again while it happens.

The writer and the pen are in the same room.
